title: Korea Has a Holiday for Its Alphabet

slides.headline: Korea takes a day off **to thank its alphabet.**
slides.note: October 9. A national holiday for 24 letters.

slides.headline: Tomorrow is **Hangeul Day**
slides.body: Hangeul Day (한글날) celebrates the Korean alphabet, Hangeul (한글). Schools and most offices close for it.

slides.headline: Before it, **reading was for elites**
slides.body: Koreans wrote in Chinese characters. Learning thousands of them took years, so most people could not read.

slides.headline: A king **made a new script**
slides.body: King Sejong (세종) and his scholars created Hangeul and published it in 1446, so ordinary people could write.

slides.headline: The letters **copy your mouth**
slides.body: Consonants are shaped like the tongue and lips that make each sound. The script was designed, not evolved.

slides.headline: Not everyone **wanted it**
slides.body: Some scholars opposed it. Chinese characters were the language of power, and an easy script threatened that.

slides.headline: Most alphabets evolved. **This one was invented.**
slides.body: Few scripts in daily use have a known creator, date and purpose. Koreans know all three for theirs.

slides.headline: Letters in **the modern alphabet**
slides.body: 14 consonants and 10 vowels. The original had 28; four dropped out of use over the centuries.

slides.headline: Learn it **before lunch**
slides.body: Its own 1446 guide says a wise person learns it in one morning. Many visitors read signs within a day.

slides.headline: Korea, explained **by a Korean.**
slides.body: Follow for the context behind the things Korea does.
slides.graphic: Seoul skyline at dusk, softly blurred behind the text.

caption:
Korea gets a national holiday every October 9 for one thing: its alphabet, Hangeul.

King Sejong published it in 1446 so ordinary people could finally read and write, and the letters are shaped like the mouth that makes each sound.

How long did it take you to learn your first alphabet?
reply: Bonus fact: Hangeul Day was dropped from the list of days off in 1991 because officials said Korea had too many holidays. People kept pushing back, and it became a day off again in 2013. What does your country celebrate that people elsewhere find surprising?
fact_check: 2장: 한글날은 공휴일. 'most offices close'는 관공서·대부분 회사 기준.
6장: 최만리 등 집현전 일부 학자의 반대 상소(1444). 이름은 생략.
8장: 현대 기본 자모 24자(자음 14, 모음 10), 창제 당시 28자.
9장: 훈민정음 해례본 정인지 서문 '슬기로운 사람은 아침을 마치기 전에, 어리석은 사람도 열흘이면 배운다'. 'many visitors read signs within a day'는 흔한 설명이라 단정 피함.
댓글: 1991년 공휴일 제외(1990년 결정, 1991년부터), 2013년 공휴일 재지정.
